summary: Australian super lightweight Liam Paro says he has no time for "schoolyard bullsh*t" after a 2019 sparring clip with WBC lightweight champion Shakur Stevenson was circulated, and says he would spar Stevenson again. The article also covers Paro's stalled 2023, with a facial fracture and an Achilles injury costing him a fight and a world title shot. He now returns against Montana Love in San Francisco on December 9, aiming to restart a world title charge.
one_line: Liam Paro shrugs off a leaked Shakur Stevenson sparring clip and prepares for his return against Montana Love on December 9 after an injury-hit 2023.
key_facts: A video of Liam Paro sparring WBC lightweight champion Shakur Stevenson was circulated after Stevenson sent it to Bill Haney, father of Devin Haney.
The clip surfaced while Stevenson was under fire for his cautious win over Edwin De Los Santos, a fight that broke the record for fewest punches landed over a 12-round contest.
Paro says the clip is from 2019, is only 45 seconds out of 240 minutes of sparring, and that he and Stevenson have sparred over 80 rounds.
Paro says he would still spar Stevenson again if needed, calling him probably one of the best, if not the best, southpaw around.
Paro knocked out Brock Jarvis in the first round last October.
Paro's March fight with Robbie Davies Jnr in Liverpool was cancelled after a routine CT scan found an unknown facial fracture and the commission ruled him out.
Paro withdrew from a June world title shot against Regis Pregrais in New Orleans because of an Achilles tendon issue, and temporarily relocated to his hometown of Mackay.
Paro, 27, faces Ohio's Montana Love in San Francisco on December 9 (Dec. 10 in Australia), on the undercard of Haney vs. Prograis for the WBC super lightweight title.
Love lost by disqualification last October after throwing Stevie Spark out of the ring in frustration.
Paro plans to bring smart pressure to Love, saying he is better in every aspect except wrestling.
Paro was previously ranked number one by the WBO at super lightweight but is now 11th because of inactivity.
Paro wants to fight three times in 2024 and says he has only had one round in two years.
